analysis.evidence: וַאֲנִי sets the speaker apart at the start of the verse. הִנְנִי מֵקִים then resumes the first person and states what he undertakes to do: establish his covenant with the addressees and their descendants.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ, “and,” prefixes the independent first-person common singular pronoun אֲנִי, “I.”
analysis.sense: I, as for me (the speaker set apart)

analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: God says מֵקִים אֶת בְּרִיתִי, “I am establishing my covenant.” The phrases אִתְּכֶם and וְאֶת זַרְעֲכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם identify Noah and his sons, together with their descendants, as covenant partners.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular noun in the construct state with a first-person singular possessive suffix referring to God, the speaker.
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh

analysis.evidence: God establishes his covenant with Noah and his sons and with זַרְעֲכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם, “your descendants after you.” The plural suffix refers to the addressees, and אַחֲרֵיכֶם identifies the generations that follow them.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with a second-person masculine plural possessive suffix. The singular noun refers collectively to descendants.
